subject: CrescentBank: scope tradeoffs & timeline for data-residency + routing shim
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CrescentBank - scope tradeoffs & timeline for data-residency + routing shim

Team — quick context: CrescentBank (prospect) is at an advanced procurement stage. Sara from Procurement flagged two non-negotiables: (1) data residency / tenancy segregation for PCI-adjacent logs, and (2) per-customer routing isolation for inference (they want logical isolation + auditability). Their legal/compliance team needs evidence before the exec sign-off; procurement has asked for a concrete timeline and limited acceptance criteria by EOW.

They are targeting a Q2 pilot and will decide on a 12–18 month license if we can meet a minimal set of requirements in time. The upsell is meaningful (~$360k ARR initial commit) but we need Product/Eng to weigh the requested scope and suggest a minimal safe path to close.

Must-haves (customer):
- Tenant-level routing isolation (requests for CRES must not be mixed with multi-tenant pool without contractual guarantees)
- Audit export (per-request trace logs) for 90 days
- SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning

Nice-to-haves:
- Dedicated pre-warmed nodes for peak hours
- On-prem option later in roadmap

Ask: Product & Eng — can you give a short bulleted assessment (feasibility, lowest-effort temporary shim, rough ETA, and any gating constraints) by EOD Jan 16? I attached the MATP requirements Sara sent and a draft SOW to work from. If we can scope a 4–6 week pilot with controls and a signed SOW, procurement is willing to accept an SLA exception fee.

Attachments: Crescent_MATP_requirements.pdf, SOW-draft-v1.docx

Thanks —
Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CrescentBank - scope tradeoffs & timeline for data-residency + routing shim

Thanks for the context, Olga — and thanks Sara (copied here) for sending the MATP. High level reaction from Product: feasible with caveats. Summarizing options so Sales has clear tradeoffs to present.

Option A — Minimal 'routing shim' (fast follow, ~3–5 wks)
- Implement a request metadata tag + routing rule that pins CRES traffic to an isolated pool (logical isolation, shared infra).
- Provide per-request trace export (log streaming to customer S3) and a contractual commitment for 90-day retention.
- SAML/SCIM work is standard integration (~1–2 wks).
- Pros: fastest to ship, keeps host model and runtime unchanged.
- Cons: not full physical separation; longer-term audits may ask for tenancy proofs.

Option B — Dedicated tenant nodes (more work, ~8–12 wks)
- Provision dedicated dedicated GPU pool, tenancy pinning, extra monitoring, and per-tenant KV sharding.
- Pros: stronger audit posture.
- Cons: materially higher operational cost and lead time; needs infra allocation.

Important constraints:
- We cannot promise on-prem in the pilot window.
- Audit exports: we can stream structured traces but will need contract language for retention and access.

Questions for Sales / CrescentBank:
1) Would Crescent accept a logical isolation + contractual guarantees for 4–6 week pilot?
2) Are there specific encryption/KMS requirements (bring-your-own-key) for the pilot?
3) Is the pilot traffic expected to be bursty (peak qps) or steady? We need QPS profile to size the pool.

If Crescent confirms acceptance of Option A for pilot, Eng will scope and commit to a target ship date by Jan 19.

—Ben
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CrescentBank - scope tradeoffs & timeline for data-residency + routing shim

Thanks — adding engineering detail and a realistic effort split.

Assumptions: pilot uses our hosted runtime, model variants are pre-approved and no model retraining required. Customer provides sample workloads and a QPS profile.

Work items for Option A (approx effort):
- Request routing tag + policy engine rule + routing to an isolated tenant pool: 5 engineer-days (backend)
- Per-request structured trace export (JSON lines + metadata) and S3 delivery hook: 4 engineer-days
- SAML/SCIM integration test plan and template connectors: 3 engineer-days (we can reuse existing connectors)
- End-to-end QA + canary + rollout plan + runbooks: 4 engineer-days
- Observability + cost meter per-tenant: 3 engineer-days

Total: ~19 engineer-days (concurrent across 2 engineers → ~10 working days calendar) plus scheduling for pre-warming infra.

Engineering caveats:
- We can do token-level isolation and routing quickly, but audit teams occasionally request physical separation. If procurement asks for stronger cryptographic separation, that pushes to Option B and ~8–12 weeks.
- We will need a signed SOW and a deal commit >$250k ARR to prioritize the infra allocation queue (this is the gating threshold we have been using).

Deliverable proposal for Sales to negotiate with Crescent:
- 4-week pilot under Option A (logical routing shim + trace exports + SSO)
- Explicit acceptance criteria: successful trace exports, no cross-tenant trace leakage, and documented access controls
- Pilot cost: monthly pilot surcharge to cover dedicated pre-warm and monitoring (we can propose a pass-through or a fixed fee)

If Sales confirms Crescent will accept Option A + pilot surcharge, we can start next Monday (Jan 26) and target a production canary by Feb 23.

—Priyom
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: CrescentBank - scope tradeoffs & timeline for data-residency + routing shim

Ben/Priyom/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. I'm looping Crescent procurement in here to confirm they will accept Option A as a pilot path and the pilot surcharge. Sara — per Product/Eng: we can deliver a logical routing shim + SAML/SCIM + trace exports as the pilot. Engineering estimates ~10 calendar days of active work across two engineers and a 4-week pilot schedule if we get a signed SOW and the pilot surcharge to prioritize infra.

Proposed next steps for Crescent to approve:
1) Sign the attached SOW-draft (we can iterate)
2) Confirm pilot QPS profile and whether BYOK/KMS is required
3) Confirm acceptance of contractual audit export retentions (90 days)

If you confirm these three items by Jan 22, we will slot the work for Jan 26 start.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.docx

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@crescentbank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CrescentBank - scope tradeoffs & timeline for data-residency + routing shim

Olga — thanks for the clear plan and to the team for the estimates. CrescentBank is amenable to Option A for the pilot provided we receive the SOW and the pilot includes:
- 90-day trace retention (we will verify)
- Dedicated routing logical isolation (we understand this is logical for pilot)
- A pilot surcharge; procurement requests the dollar amount to be listed in the SOW.

We will get finance sign-off this week if the SOW is in place. Please send a DocuSign link and a line-item for the pilot surcharge and we'll aim to return a countersigned SOW by Jan 23.

Sara Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager
CrescentBank
